source.title: Performance of Time-series Momentum Strategy: US Evidence

quoted:
Abstract: This paper examines the effectiveness of the time series momentum strategy in 
generating positive returns in the US stock market, with a focus on exploring its dynamics

The motivation behind this study is to examine the effectiveness of the time series momentum 
strategy in generating positive returns in the US stock market, as well as to explore its dynamics and 
performance using different moving average methods. Specifically, this paper aims to investigate the

signal_construction.value: The signal is constructed using a linear regression model to predict future returns. The factors (ft) in the model are either Simple Moving Averages (MA) or Exponential Moving Averages (EMA) of past returns. The lookback period (N) for these moving averages is set to 24. Portfolio weights are then calculated based on the moving average, regression coefficients (alpha and beta), and expected volatility (sigma squared).
signal_construction.note: The paper uses a regression model to predict returns, where factors are MA or EMA. The lookback period N is 24. Portfolio weights are derived from these predictions.

what_is_missing: Detailed trading rules (e.g., specific entry/exit signals, position sizing beyond portfolio weights).
A robust market impact model for transaction costs, instead of fixed rates.
Analysis of latency or execution considerations for the strategy.
Discussion of the specific assets within the S&P500 (e.g., large-cap vs. small-cap, sector biases).
The paper notes overfitting to the training data but does not propose specific methods to mitigate it within the study.

transposability.what_transfers: The general concept of time-series momentum using moving averages (MA/EMA) as signals. The importance of evaluating strategies with and without transaction costs. The finding that simpler strategies (like Equal Weight) can be more robust under higher transaction costs. The methodology of using a regression model to predict returns based on moving average factors could be adapted.
what_does_not_transfer: The specific universe of S&P500 constituent stocks, as our focus is on intraday futures.
The daily data frequency, as our universe is intraday.
The fixed transaction cost rates (0.001, 0.005, 0.01) are not representative of real-world market impact for intraday futures trading.
The lookback period of N=24 days is too long for an intraday strategy.
The observed overfitting to the training data suggests the model might not generalize well to different market conditions or asset classes without further refinement.
transposability.what_aligns_well: The paper's emphasis on the critical role of transaction costs in determining profitability. The comparison of different moving average types (MA vs. EMA) and their varying performance. The evaluation of strategies on an out-of-sample test set. The observation that strategies with lower turnover rates might perform better with higher transaction costs.
